chapterTitle: Chapter 1: The Winged Whales resting ground (Ceres)
editorText:
“Eeerr Thanks Tao, much appreciated”, Shai shot up out of her seat awkwardly making her way to the front of the horseshoe, lightly stepping to the middle of the class where John had rested the suit’s helmet. The suit stood strong next to the desk now, an open shell waiting for it’s next occupant. As John made his way back to end of the horseshoe, He lifted his hand and patted Shai on the shoulder as she passed him by, she let out a little thank-you smile, followed by a deep breath, she hated public talking, but she also took pride in her craft, she got a great sense of satisfaction form sharing her knowledge with the others.

“Ok! so Deep space medicine varies a little differently to your standard medicine, and as I am sure you are all aware, having lived on Ceres you have done this training more times than you can remember'', Shai spoke with deliverance in her message, then paused momentarily “But.. Complacency is the killer..” She concluded softly resting her hands in each other. She no longer seemed awkward the deeper she got into her field.

She knelt down in front of the suit, her small frame seemingly smaller before the scale of the armoured giant.  Shai detached a matt white vambrace from the suit’s forearm .The brace had a blue cross on it’s side, what had become the universal symbol for a Deep Space Kit (DSK) med kit, Specifically designed for the Deep Space Medic or ‘DSM’ as she explained it. The DSK didn’t contain standard bandages or Gauss. It had been designed for zero gravity situations.

The braces thickness and solid gloss finish made it feel and looked like an angelic piece of armour crafted by the heavens, although it was something else in its design, much more if used properly by it’s occupant. Shai held the bracer out in front of her “Has anyone used a DSK Medi-Guard?” she caressed the shell of the vambrace, running her finger down its white glossy finish. “The Medi-Guard comes stock standard with the Mark IV suit. Most of its operation is intuitive and based off your suits vital monitoring systems linked through your cerebral gate”

Shai admired the beauty of the system. She seemed possessed, as she slowly rose from her knee. She took the brace in both her palms and continued. “For the most part the unit is autonomous, although the under belly does have a hold for manual administration, and it’s drug stores are removable like so” Shai pressed her finger on a small latch removing a seamless cover from the brace. Underneath a series of pipes fed into a stack of vials that surrounded the braces inner shroud.

She plucked one of the vials from it’s holder and inserted it into a syringe in a fluid motion, “So that they can be administered by trained persons” She pressed the syringe needle into a square replica of human intramuscular tissue, injecting the contents of the vial.

“What happens if the module gets taken out by incoming fire” Tex, folded his arms, a slight smirk rocking back in his chair, his head slightly tilted forward.. “Good question Tex” Shai said softly. “If the module takes damage it’s fine” She continued almost unmoved by the big guy’s question, re coupling the DSK back to the suits forearm folding it over the vambrace and locking it back in place. “The vambrace merely acts as a backup module for easy access and patient treatments. There is a physical separate overlay in your HUD, If the DSK has been damaged, Don’t worry too much, all of the core programming for the neuro-swap run’s from your neural implant in synchronous function with your suit. The helmet’s HUD can also be used to select pre-programmed procedures.

Nano-Bot holding bays are built into the suits rear around the lower abdomen, Heart analysis and sounding is performed  through an augmented chest cavity with listeners, coupled to your cerebral link from your implant, appropriate medicinal inputs are distributed through a venous injection mesh spanning the entirety of the suit, all of which is controlled by one central point, the helmets computer. The bracer, simply acts as a backup for field deployment if all else fails. All the knick knacks to keep you going in the thick of it, are stored in the lower rear of the suits backed armour plating, so it is completely safe. Measured dosages are automatically placed into injection ports in the suit. These Injection ports feed through an intricately woven path through the suit that follows much the same pattern as the nervous system. Think of your veins for instance, they have hundreds of gates. This system is assessed by your suit’s inbuilt nerve scanners. If you are injured the suit performs a measured intramuscular injection of adrenaline, or be it paralysis to an affected limb, the injection needle acts as a channel for nerve tendrons which take over and act in place of severed nerves to bridge gaps in motor function through nerve damage. The suit gives you a temporary backup nervous system, and its actuators can still function even if you have taken neural damage to your muscular, or spinal system”.

Shai went quiet for a moment, pondering “I wonder what the limits and protections are built into this thing if a cognitive hack takes place, but who would have the technology to do such a thing, commandeer our own autonomous system through our suits? I need to check this with Tao later” Shai wasn’t entirely convinced of the helmets security protection, it didn’t cover all grounds, or sleeper programs that could be laid when the suits are sent out of production.

She looked concerned for a minute, then resumed back to her lesson. “So, to summarize. In a traumatic situation, the suit’s integrated neural mesh with equipped motor response actuators offers crucial medical response benefits. The neural integration enables a more natural and intuitive control over the suits movements. This enhances coordination and suit responsiveness, eliminating any delays of the earlier kinematic models. This is especially valuable for individuals that may sustain impaired motor functions during a conflict,  allowing them to regain mobility and independence in the fight.

Additionally, the neural interface facilitates better synchronization between your intentions and the suit, reducing cognitive effort to operate the suit. This is also vital in high-stress situations. Overall the effectiveness of this suit is ahead of its time in medical and emergency scenarios and you my friends, will basically have a walking life suit until we can get you to a med bay to repair any severed tissue. This suit will get you home” Shai rose from her pose of admiration where she had knelt in front of the suit’s shell, she had been holding in her elbows the new helmet cradling it like a child, gazing into the chip integration pad that was recessed into the titanium mesh at the back of the helmet. She appeared like a mother before the class, and they felt embraced to have such a knowledgeable medic with them.

John sat patiently observing Shai, she was so nimble, yet her mind was beautiful to him, he smiled knowing how safe his team would be with her watching over them. “Shai, so tell us about the buddy system feature, the one that’s paired with each suit”, “Yes Cap!” Shai woke from her deep thoughts and returned to the room. “When an injured ally has taken damage these suits have a neural link system, So say if we need to utilize a certain skill set we don’t have as long as someone with the skills are in range they can piggy back onto the suits backup neurological pathway and in essence hijack the suit, to well get you out of a pickle. Think of it like swapping suits really”.

Tau lent in with edging curiosity, “So you are saying we can swap bodies?”.Tex let out a cheeky smirk, “I’ve always wondered what it would be like to have control over a woman's body, can we do a test run?”, Tau rolled her eyes with slight amusement. “Focus guys!” Shot John.

Shai continued pretending to be uninterrupted. “The big guy actually raises a good point. The suit doesn’t allow you to swap bodies as such Tex.. It just projects your motor commands onto the other suit and if you permit it your suit will take their commands over yours, You can choose a two way bridge or a one way which may be the case if your friend is unconscious... It isn’t a body swap as such, but a suit swap. Because these suits no longer rely on Kinematic but cerebral actuation, The cerebral gate intercepts signals from the host projecting it to the required suit via it’s home suit’s telemetry unit, as long as it is within range. Once you have used your own suit long enough, your synapse profile will be projected with your cerebral communications hand in hand. So even though your host may have a better knee than you or a kink in his elbows connective tissue, you will experience your neural commands all the same regardless of the suit you commandeer”

Tau cut in. “It is a little jumpy at first if you have never synced with a suit before though as each suit needs to adjust for different neural signal latencies of different hosts.. So tonight your rides may be a little bumpy while it smooths out your synapse profile, So don’t get to cocky on the outer hull with the first run”, “Thanks Tau” said Shai.

“Obviously if a swap is performed with an unconscious ally your suit will be incapacitated taking on their state. So I would advise thinking things through before establishing the bridge. On that thought.. Guys would it be worth using the Mark IV’s new auto targeting system in this case?”, “Nice pickup Shai!” Tao was impressed with Shai’s lateral thinking. “I’ll jot down a note and get to work on putting that feature into the suits programming tonight, then forward it onto engineering for testing”. “I took the liberty of setting a reminder for you Miss Vang” Chimed Kitten.

“Ok I think it’s time we gave the legs a stretch” John piped in with a soft smile. “Sure Cap, I’ll let you run through the pre-walk checks” Shai bowled slightly at the captain, stepping aside to the air lock panel and began prepping the interlock over the panel.
